utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. You may sit down, please. Yes, Mr. Seric. Direct examination, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Thank you very much, Mr. President. I will be an optimist and say that I hope I'll finish my direct examination by 7.00. Examined by Mr. Seric:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, you will now be shown a piece of paper with your name on it and the pseudonym that has been given you. So tell Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. us, please, if that is indeed your name, but don't read it out.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MF
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you follow my question and wait with your answer, believe me, we shall make headway than if you rush too much, because the interpreters need to interpret it all. The best thing to do is look at the light on my microphone. And can the technical booth please bring the microphone down so I can see the witness. Witness, I will first ask you certain things about yourself and will invite you to give us some particulars about yourself.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: So, Mr. President, can we go into private session, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. We'll go to the private session, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you called up?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MF
utterances.text: No, I wasn't. I never did any military service. I wasn't fit for the army.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember the time when the conflict started between the BH army and the HVO? It was on the 9th of May, 1993. What is it that you heard at that day? What did you experience that day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MF
utterances.text: I heard a lot of noise and some unknown people expelled me to the left bank, me, my wife, and one of my daughters.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know who were the soldiers? Whose unit was it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MF
utterances.text: I have no idea. I didn't --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And where were you accommodated on this bank of Mostar?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MF
utterances.text: In Mahala, in lower, Donja Mahala.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when did you return to your apartment?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MF
utterances.text: I was there 22 days and then they returned us back to the apartment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you run into problems again after you returned to your apartment?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MF
utterances.text: Yes. On the 2nd of July, 1993, when they came again and took me to the Heliodrom, again people I didn't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know which unit those soldiers belonged to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MF
utterances.text: I have no idea.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How were you taken away? In what way?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MF
utterances.text: They simply came, they left the elderly, and my wife, and my daughter, and took me away, those unknown men.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And where were you put in the Heliodrom?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MF
utterances.text: In the school.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what were the conditions there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MF
utterances.text: Well, we had a meal a day, and -- there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many of you were in one room?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MF
utterances.text: In one room, ten of us to a room. Ten to a room.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you mistreated, I mean you personally?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MF
utterances.text: No, I was not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what about others who were with you in that group?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MF
utterances.text: I don't know. I have no idea. We dared not anything.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see any bruises on them, any scars?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MF
utterances.text: No. I -- nothing. We did not ... We did not dare.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you taken for labour?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MF
utterances.text: I was taken only once, on the 28th of August, 1993.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And where? What happened then?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MF
utterances.text: I was taken next to Carinski Most Bridge, and we carried sacks, and a shell hit there and I was wounded there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where were you wounded? What part of your body?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MF
utterances.text: Part of my arm and my right leg.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And after you were wounded, what happened then? Were you taken somewhere?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MF
utterances.text: Yes. To the surgical ward in the hospital in Mostar.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how long did you -- were you in the hospital?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MF
utterances.text: Until the 5th of September, 1993.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And after that day, where did you go then?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MF
utterances.text: My wife came to fetch me and we returned to our flat, where we had been before.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And after that, were you still afraid for your safety?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MF
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you turn to anyone for help?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MF
utterances.text: I did. Mr. Vinko Martinovic, Stela, and his father, Ivan.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why Vinko Martinovic of all people?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MF
utterances.text: Because Vinko Martinovic was not afraid of anyone, and I turned to him, my wife and I, because my wife was very ill. She had had an operation. And had it not been for him and his parents, I don't know what would have happened.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And on what terms were you on general with Ivan and Vinko's brother, and Vinko?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MF
utterances.text: Good, always.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know anything about what his attitude to Muslims was, those that you knew and in your neighbourhood?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MF
utterances.text: Nobody complained. He helped everybody, old people and children, and I shall never forget it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know what duty did he have in the army?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MF
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was his unit like? Where was it quartered?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MF
utterances.text: It was on Kalemova Street.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, do you want a short break? Would you like some water? I see that you are upset. All right. We shall break for a moment, and I have two more questions and I'll be finished. Don't be afraid. Nobody Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. will bite you here, nobody will beat you.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MF
utterances.text: My first time. I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, perhaps I was too fast. Perhaps it sounded like cross-examination rather than direct. But it will be over in no time. So did Vinko's father, Ivan, also help you and your family?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MF
utterances.text: He helped me a lot, he and his family, the whole family.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I have no further questions in my direct examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Witness, I understand that it's difficult for someone who came from far away to give his testimony in this courtroom. If you are not feeling good, we could stop here and we'll continue tomorrow. I see Mr. Seric is nodding. Witness, I have to remind you that during your stay in The Hague, you are still under the oath, so do not talk to anybody and do not let anybody talk to you about your testimony.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I won't.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: And we'll resume our sitting tomorrow morning at 9.00 in the courtroom 2. Mr. Usher, would you please show the witness out of the room, please. Mr. Seric, are there any health problems with this witness, or he just, you know, unfamiliar with the situation in this courtroom?

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, he was informed about the situation in the courtroom. No, he does not have any health problems. But he's terribly afraid and he is very -- I told him about the technical problems and all the -- all this, but he's never been to a court, in whatever capacity, and he looks like an elderly person but he's not that old at all. It's just that kind of man. He's been through what he's been through, and his family too, but he wanted to testify here. The man is simply afraid. He has stage fever. He's a bit withdrawn, not difficult to get to, and that is why I tried to cut it short, not to bother him too much, and I hope my learned friend will not keep him too long. Thank you very much for inquiring.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DIARRA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But tomorrow morning you will have to ask him to speak into the microphone, his head is just too low and he speaks at the table. He must be reassured somehow that people here are not mean, that they won't harm him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I hope Mr. Bos will bear that in mind.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: I'll try to keep the witness's head up, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. We'll rise now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
